# Technology surges

Each technological revolution (canals, railways, electricity, the car, the chip) unfolds over roughly half a century and in two halves.

## Installation

Financial capital falls in love with the new technology. Money floods in, infrastructure is overbuilt, and a bubble forms. Most of the early companies fail, but the network they financed remains.

## Turning point

The bubble bursts. There is a recession and an argument about regulation.

## Deployment

Production capital takes over. The technology becomes cheap, boring and universal, and the gains spread through the rest of the economy.

Compare the older and looser idea of [[Kondratiev waves]].
